title: Luxury Car Dashboard Time Dilation Simulator
description: A concept car sits on a reflective surface with a giant Rolex watch mounted on its dashboard. The user controls the car's velocity using a slider, and as the car accelerates toward the speed of light, the Rolex's second hand visibly slows down demonstrating relativistic time dilation. Users can also toggle between the car's reference frame and an external observer frame to compare clock speeds.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 that implements a relativistic time dilation physics demonstration. Load both GLB assets using GLTFLoader from a CDN. Place the CarConcept model centered on a large reflective ground plane. Scale and position the Rolex model so it appears mounted on or floating just above the car's dashboard area, clearly visible. Set up a PerspectiveCamera at a 3/4 front angle showing both the car and the watch face. Add an HDR-style lighting setup with a DirectionalLight, ambient light, and a subtle SpotLight illuminating the watch face. Create a ground plane with MeshStandardMaterial using moderate metalness and roughness for reflections. Implement these interactions: Step 1 - A velocity slider (0% to 99.9% speed of light) controls the car's simulated speed. Step 2 - As velocity increases, animate the Rolex second hand rotation speed using the Lorentz factor gamma = 1/sqrt(1 - v^2/c^2), making the hand tick slower at higher velocities. If the Rolex model has no separable hand, create a thin red needle mesh overlaid on the watch face and rotate it. Step 3 - Display a real-time HUD overlay showing current velocity as percentage of c, the Lorentz factor gamma, and elapsed proper time vs coordinate time. Step 4 - A toggle button switches between Observer Frame where the camera stays fixed and the car shakes subtly with particle streaks showing motion, and Car Frame where the camera parents to the car and the environment color-shifts toward blue via post-processing tint. Step 5 - At velocities above 90% c, add a visual length contraction effect by scaling the car along its forward axis by 1/gamma. Use OrbitControls for free camera rotation. Animate everything in the render loop with a clock delta. Style the UI controls with a dark semi-transparent panel fixed at the bottom of the screen.
